levels.title: Check Small Even Cases
levels.body_md: Look closely at your even check in main. It is correct for large inputs but not for every small input. What is the smallest even weight that can really be split into two valid parts?
levels.question_back: What is the smallest even weight that can really be split?

levels.title: Positive Parts Need Minimum Sum
levels.body_md: The key idea is positive even parts. Each part must be at least two, so the total cannot be too small. Think about the minimum possible sum of two such parts.

levels.title: Your Even Check Is Incomplete
levels.body_md: Your bug is on `L6`. That line accepts any even `w` using only `w % 2 == 0`. It forgets that both parts must be positive, so the smallest even weight slips through.

levels.title: Require Weight Above Two
levels.body_md: You need two parts that are both positive and even. That means each part is at least `2`, so their sum is at least `4`. Your current `L6` returns YES for the smallest even weight, but it can only split as one plus one. Keep your same structure and output, just also require on `L6` that the weight is larger than two. This stays `O(1)` time and `O(1)` memory.
